context_coverage: The contract administrator is inspecting the completed building to decide whether to issue the practical completion certificate despite a list of 47 snagging items still outstanding.

The employer wants to take possession of a completed wing of a phased hospital project before the rest of the building is finished, and the contractor disputes whether sectional completion provisions apply.
Practical completion was certified 3 months late due to the contractor's programme overrun, and the employer is seeking to deduct liquidated damages at the rate stated in the contract.
The contractor is claiming that practical completion was achieved on the programmed date even though the certificate was not issued, arguing the employer had beneficial use of the building.
The defects liability period begins at practical completion, and the contractor needs to understand when their obligation to return and remedy defects formally expires.
